# Policy-KB bijection audit — cgm_sensor_supply_services / task 1

Scope: `cgm_ext_model_change_authorization_units`, `cgm_ext_payment_plan_installment`, `cgm_ext_plan_member_waiver_units` and `cgm_ext_model_change_refill_units` (charter_scope of task 1); the base policies they name (`cgm_documentation_and_authorization`, `cgm_continued_coverage_visits`, `cgm_evt_refill_shipment`, `cgm_evt_quantity_limits`, `cgm_holds_and_closure`, `cgm_evt_patient_account`, `cgm_combo_pump_compatibility`, `cgm_liability_notice`); the tier parameters; and the contracts of the four task tools. Done after the blind freeze. Doc meta was used only to locate homes.

### Differences
- **KB-1 (KB-BIJECTION RED, low; scoring unaffected in this task).** Three refill factor documents compress the third tier, which the source states as a computation rule, into "this rule does not apply". The tier's method is then absent from its own factor document.
  - `doc_cgm_refill_draw_frequency_edit_bulletin` rule 3: "When no remittance for that claim has posted, or the latest refill was never claimed, this edit has no remittance to read and no such marking by it applies." Source `refill_frequency_rule` tier 3: "every block, when the paid supply runs past today" (rule: "otherwise every block of the delivery is at risk when that paid supply runs past today"). "No such marking" also admits a zero-blocks-at-risk reading, which is opposite to the source. The sibling waiver doc `doc_cgm_waiver_frequency_edit` rule 3 states the tier in full.
  - `doc_cgm_refill_draw_ship_timing_rule` rule 3: "In every other case neither of these timing rules applies." Source `superseded_refill_timing` tier 3: "lead days before its ship date plus its supply days". The same doc says the in-scope earliest date "is set by the timing rules of this shipping rule", so the in-scope fall-through date is not given in this doc. The waiver doc `doc_cgm_waiver_earliest_ship_date` rule 3 states it.
  - `doc_cgm_refill_draw_waiver_coverage_memo` §2 rule 3: "Otherwise, with no plan member waiver for the item on the program, no waiver coverage applies." Source `waiver_coverage_rule` tier 3 (rule text): "otherwise the delivery ships only when it has no exposed units".
  - In each case the computation document carries a baseline equal to the tier (clauses 5, 7 and 6 of `…units_billing_manual`), so a reader who falls back to it gets the source number. Task 1 hits tier 1 of all three. The renderer's own note ("refill says 'no such marking applies', same meaning") is judged under R-note below.

## dependency_form

- All four prerequisite sentences are verbatim in documents of their blocked policies; the restatements are same-form (state). None is in a depended-on policy's documents.
- Hubs name only their own tools. There is no route, checklist, aggregated chain, ordered multi-problem list, wrong/right contrast, or FAQ walking across problems.
- Titles are general subjects. "Model Change Authorization Grants…" and "Superseded Sensor Supply on Model Change Grants" name the policy's own defining subject, a new order that changes the model. None restates "ship my first box today".
- Factor docs: none says which tier customers fall on. Computation docs carry no variation hint.
- Sibling-policy naming in `doc_cgm_refill_draw_hardship_posting_terms` §1 ("the same ship-time test under the program's plan member waiver rule"), `doc_cgm_waiver_hardship_set_aside` ("the refill count made on a change of CGM model and of the plan member waiver count") and the holds retired clause. This is the shared holds replaced_by verbatim. It states no dependency and names no tool, so it is source-side (S-3), not RED.
- Factor-on-factor wording in `doc_cgm_statement_cycle_installment` ("the pump balance taken in") and `doc_cgm_pump_plan_installment_carve` ("comes off the Insulin Pump Program balance counted in the … plan"). This is the source's own assembly sentence ("plus the pump balance taken in less its waiting postings and the pump plan's left-out installments, never below zero for the pump part"), so it is source-side (S-1/S-2).
- **KB-2 (KB-EXPLICIT RED, low): scored value in a hub illustration.** `doc_cgm_model_change_grant_recording` § Return: "*Hypothetical illustration of the receipt shape:* 'Authorization auth_… recorded on enrollment … for A4239 under payer PA …: 4 unit(s), valid … through …'". The task-1 scored `units_authorized` for this tool is 4 (evaluation_criteria). The doc calls it a placeholder, but it puts the scored figure on the very tool the solver must call, and a solver may copy it instead of deriving it. The value has no source home; the source has no illustration.

**KB-EXPLICIT RED** (KB-2).

The KB kept the docs independent by defining the shortened paid supply in the allowance doc. |

The KB follows the compute. |
| R-5 | CONFIRMED (source) | `superseded_supply_overlap.ladder[0]` and the rule say the record "documents that the pump requires the new model"; compute `overlap_blocks` tests only `justification_date >= pump_delivery_date`. No record field carries that content. |

| R-7 | CONFIRMED (source) | Rule "the delivery draws on the newest grant", with no ordering; compute `newest_grant_id` = `LATEST(... date_field='valid_through')`, so only the latest-valid-through grant is tested. The KB grant-draw doc pins it ("whose valid-through date is the latest"). |
| R-8 | CONFIRMED (source) | Compute `insulin_closed_date = '9999-12-31'` unless stopped insulin, so no credit ever. The rule's "…on or after the date … closed when the customer has stopped insulin" can be read as a date test for stopped customers only. The KB states the compute reading. |
| R-9 | CONFIRMED (source wording) | Rule "paid part"; compute `SUM(payer_paid_amount) > 0` (full payment included). The KB defines "paid part" as total above zero. |
| R-10 | CONFIRMED (source wording; no reachable effect) | Compute `P('past_due_hold_days') // 30`. In-scope tiers have 90, 120 or 0 days, all exact multiples; only Self-Pay (15) has a fraction, and it is outside both policies' scope. |
| R-11 | CONFIRMED (source) | Rule "its payments"; compute `plan_covered` sums every `cgm_patient_payment` in the window. The KB waiver 3.3 / refill 9 follow the compute. |
| R-12 | CONFIRMED (source) | Compute `latest_refill_delivered … or latest_refill_ship`; the rule is silent. The KB timing docs add the fallback from the compute. |
| R-13 | CONFIRMED (source) | `waiver_coverage_rule.ladder[0..1]` "at-risk units"; rule and compute `shipped_units` use `risk_units + excess_units`. The KB follows the rule (exposed units). Decisive here: task 1's only exposed unit is a beyond-authorization unit, 0 at risk. |

| R-15 | CONFIRMED (source; latent) | `pump_waiting = MN(pump_taken_in, pump_recent_remits + pump_recent_charges …)` also in the other-coverage branch, where only charges were taken in. Task 1 bills the same coverage. |
| R-16 | CONFIRMED (trivial) | Waiver `pa_left = MX(0, …)`; the rule has no floor; no effect on any result. |
| R-17 | CONFIRMED (source) | The ABN rule/baseline speak only of "a supply whose CGM program documents a qualifying regimen"; no binding reads `insulin_regimen`, so the non-qualifying branch is undefined in the rule (compute returns 0 at risk). |
| R-18 | CONFIRMED (source; latent) | `insulin_cover_end_offset … else -9999` → `every_unit` for a stopped customer with no insulin refill; the rule does not cover this. |

| R-21 | CONFIRMED (source; latent) | `review_visit_date` → `'0000-00-00'` with no qualifying visit → months left 0 → 0 counted blocks when a horizon applies; the rule does not cover this. |

### XF class — every member across the six policies (one list)
XF here means a computation document that names a factor-only quantity (or tells the reader a variation exists), or a factor document that names another factor's quantity. For each member: KB location → source sentence it renders.

1. **Renewal, computation doc** `doc_cgm_renewal_grant_billing_units` R-1.3 and its clause list ("the review starts on the later of the review visit date and the regimen change date; the months left in the horizon …; … times the sum of the counted blocks and the bridge") → compute_basis `review_start_date`/`review_months_left`/`authorized_blocks`/`result` (= R2-1).
2. **Renewal, computation doc** R-1.3 clause 1 ("with neither on record, the review start is earlier than every record, and no month of a horizon is left") → the tail of compute_basis `review_visit_date`/`treating_visits`/`signer_visits` (= R2-2). The factor doc `…review_visit_practitioner` does not carry this tail.
3. **Renewal, computation doc** R-1.2 table rows "Next refill date", "Grant still valid on the order date", "Units left on the item's grants", "Stopped insulin" → compute_basis `order_date`… shared reading and `insulin_stopped`. These inputs are read only by `refill_bridge`, `span_start_anchor` and `coverage_review_horizon`.
4. **ABN, computation doc** `doc_cgm_abn_unit_count_billing_manual` 4.1 "Stopped insulin" → compute_basis `insulin_stopped` (unbound, read only by `coverage_risk_scope`/`prior_notice_credit`).
5. **ABN, computation doc** 4.4 "The next delivery carries the fewest of its sized blocks …" → compute_basis `next_delivery_units` ("sized blocks" = `exposure_limited_delivery`).
6. **MC, computation doc** `doc_cgm_model_change_grant_unit_count` 1.5 "the billing units per 30 days the order supports … the counted blocks less the blocks taken off the grant" → compute_basis `result` ("…the order supports … less the deducted blocks and the blocks the follow-up visit requirement removes"). The KB wording is softened to "taken off". Borderline member.
7. **Payment plan, computation doc** `doc_cgm_installment_amount_worksheet` §1 (recent postings) and §2. The plan balance "less the amounts left out of the plan … less the program's postings that wait for the next statement, plus the part taken in from the customer's Insulin Pump Program", with the three pump cases and "installments left out under its own approved payment plan", plus three pump worked figures → compute_basis `covered_balance`/`cgm_unpaid` (= R2-5).
8. **Payment plan, computation doc** worksheet §2 last paragraph ("For a plan priced on this worksheet … can take in the balance of the customer's Insulin Pump Program") → overwrite replaced_by tail (round-1 O-2, moved).
9. **Waiver, source baseline** `baseline.rule` "…the paid-supply end is the latest refill's ship date plus its paid supply days, less the early-refill allowance" beside "No early-refill allowance applies" → KB `doc_cgm_waiver_unit_count` 2.1 renders the plain form (no allowance). This is a source-only member and the KB is clean (= R2-7).
10. **Refill, source baseline** the same `baseline.rule` sentence, and compute_basis `risk_units` "the at-risk blocks less the excepted blocks" → KB `doc_cgm_refill_draw_units_billing_manual` 2 and 5 render the plain form. Source-only member, KB clean (= R2-7).

Not members, with the reason:
- ABN listing tier 2 "every unit left on the grant the next delivery draws on" (R2-3); ABN insulin record "listed units"; the waiver/refill exception "at-risk blocks"; waiver listing "units at risk"; refill waiver coverage "exposed units". Each names a quantity the computation doc itself defines (ABN 4.4 grant drawn and 4.2 listed units; waiver 5.1 / refill 5–6 at-risk and exposed units), which other factors modify. That is a baseline quantity, not another factor's.

Visible effect: in members 1–5, 7 and 8 the computation doc announces that a horizon, bridge, review visit, regimen change, sizing, set-asides, statement waits and a pump take-in exist, which pre-solves the factor search for them. The renewal and payment-plan computation docs also give no definite number when read alone unless every named quantity is read as zero; read that way they give the GT baselines 36 and 86.96. The source assembly / unbound compute_basis text is the cause; no placement in the KB avoids it, because in round 1 the same text in factor docs made them name each other.

### CGM Commercial HMO hold limit (for the bgm auditor)
`doc_cgm_hold_thresholds_and_limits` (not re-rendered in round 2): "CGM Commercial HMO Program | 90 | 75.00 USD | Yes | 60 | 30". The hold limit is **60 calendar days from the hold start date**. ### XF class, round 3: every member across the six policies
Criteria: XF_recipe points 1–6, applied to `baseline.rule`, non-factor `compute_basis`, `result` and every factor sentence, and to the KB carriage.

| Id | Policy | Source sentence → KB home | Point |
|---|---|---|---|
| XF3-1 | renewal | baseline.rule "…the grant's counted blocks, the blocks of its span, never exceed the months left of a coverage review, **blocks added on top of the span not counting toward that limit**" → computation doc R-1.2 (verbatim; the "When the review limit bears" reading repeats the span-only limit) | 1: the standard method states that additions exist. The only addition is the `refill_bridge` factor, so the computation-doc reader learns that a bridge-like addition exists. |
| XF3-2 | waiver | baseline.rule "the units beyond the payer authorization are, when the delivery draws on a grant other than …" → waiver computation doc 2.3 | 3: no waiver baseline step reads it ("The waiver lists the units at risk"); only `waiver_listing_scope` does. A one-factor quantity sits in the standard method. |
| XF3-2 | waiver, refill | baseline.rule "The latest refill … read for its ship date, supply days, billing route **and claim**" → waiver 2.1 / refill clause 2 and the table row "claim" | 3: only `frequency_edit_rule` / `refill_frequency_rule` read the claim. |
| XF3-2 | payment plan | baseline.rule "recent postings are those posted less than one whole calendar month before today" → worksheet §2 first bullet | 3: only `statement_cycle_window` reads recent postings (its doc defines them again). |
| XF3-2 | advance notice | baseline.rule "The latest refill … read for its … **refill confirmation date** …" → computation doc 4.1 | 3: only `listed_delivery_basis` reads it. |

Not members, with the reason:
- Generic `result` order sentences in all six computation docs: the form recipe point 4 prescribes. They name standard quantities (span, anchor, earliest ship date, paid-supply end, at-risk blocks, waiting rule, listing), not factor ids.
- Shared plain quantities read by two or more factors and defined once in the standard method (recipe point 2):
  - renewal: grant still valid / latest refill (span start, bridge)
  - ABN: "Stopped insulin" (risk scope, credit)
  - MC: "per-period approval" (approval kind, superseded supply)
  - waiver/refill: "pump delivery", "over-limit justification" (timing, exception)
  - payment plan: "the same coverage record" (pump fold, pump carve, statement cycle)
- The renewal factor docs' "the standard … applies" tier-3 wording is the source ladder's own.

Note for the coordinator: under the KB-audit skill's letter, a computation document that says adjustments exist ("Each adjustment … changes the standard … in this order") hints at variation. The recipe deliberately accepts this for the single generic `result` sentence. I record it as accepted design, not as a finding. XF3-1 goes further than the recipe allows, because it sits in `baseline.rule` and describes a specific kind of addition.
